title: Instacart adapter tracer skeleton behind the retailer-neutral interface
body:
## Role
A backend engineer building tracer code: a thin, demoable end-to-end path with stubs at the edges.

## Goal
Add an `InstacartAdapter` behind the retailer-neutral adapter interface (#144) with typed request/response boundaries and an injected transport, returning a deterministic stubbed handoff so the approval flow is demoable before any network call exists.

## Context
The adapter interface and the universal export adapter come from #144. This issue adds the second adapter. It proves the boundary holds: core modules never import Instacart types, and the adapter declares only the capability #139's ADR allows (working name `shopping_list_link`).

## Deliverables
- `grocery_butler/fulfillment/instacart/` with `models.py` (typed `ProductsLinkRequest`, `LineItem`, `Measurement`, `Filters`, `ProductsLinkResponse`), `adapter.py` (`InstacartAdapter`), and `transport.py` (a `Transport` protocol plus `FakeTransport`).
- Registration in the adapter registry, off by default (`INSTACART_ENABLED` unset means disabled).
- A stub mode that returns a fixed, clearly fake link such as `https://example.invalid/instacart-stub/<plan-version>`.

## Concrete examples
```python
adapter = InstacartAdapter(transport=FakeTransport.ok("https://example.invalid/l/abc"))
assert adapter.capabilities == {Capability.SHOPPING_LIST_LINK}
result = adapter.create_handoff(approved_plan)  # HandoffResult(kind="link", url=..., status="created")
```

## Constraints
- No real HTTP client in this issue. The production transport arrives in #148.
- Core modules don't import anything under `fulfillment/instacart`; add a test that enforces it.
- Don't claim `read_cart`, `read_order` or `import_receipt`.

## Dependencies
#144 (adapter interface), #143 (plan versions to hand off), #139 ADR for the capability name.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `InstacartAdapter` passes the shared adapter contract tests from #144.
- [ ] With Instacart disabled, the registry offers only the universal export.
- [ ] An import-boundary test fails if a core module imports the Instacart package.

## Testing requirements
Contract tests against `FakeTransport`; a test that the stub link is deterministic per plan version; the import-boundary test.

## Out of scope
Field translation (#147), credentials and real calls (#148), UI (#149).

## Documentation requirements
README Architecture: Fulfillment adapters lists Instacart as stub-only.

## Done-Done (repository requirements)
- Invoke tools through `./scripts/*`, never directly; `./scripts/check-all.sh` exits 0.
- Keep the repository's coverage, typing, lint, security and complexity thresholds; don't weaken any gate.
- No `noqa`, `type: ignore`, disabled checks, test skips or retries added to get green. A flaky test is worse than no test.
- Deterministic contract tests and negative-path tests. Tests use a fake transport; a normal test run never calls Instacart.
- Update the docs and API contracts this change touches in the same PR.
- Review the final diff for Safeway or Instacart coupling in core domain modules (`consolidator`, `pantry_manager`, `recipe_store`, `models`, `pending_actions`).
- The PR body references the epic (#142) and closes this issue.
